chains.title: GATA3 binds the alt T allele more strongly and activates a TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: GATA3 is the best-supported TF: E06 shows MCF-7 ChIP-seq occupancy over rs4784227, and E35 gives GATA3's own QBiC-SELEX model passing the gate with alt-gain (z=10.91, effect=0.783; site strength ref 83.3rd vs alt 98.0th percentile); E20 also gives a stronger CIS-BP-mapped GATA2 model (z=18.65, effect=0.283, alt more). The ChIP peak is not allele-specific, so the allelic direction is inferred from QBiC-SELEX, not shown in cells. GATA3 is chosen over other bound TFs by matching MCF-7 occupancy, very high expression (rank 5 of 1626), and an own-model QBiC alt-gain.

The variant lies in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3180851 with DNase and H3K27ac signal and active-element cofactors, so allele-specific GATA3 binding at this base could alter enhancer activity. E03 z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not MCF-7-specific, so MCF-7 enhancer activity is not directly shown.

The element is assigned to TOX3 by proximity, Open Targets L2G, and literature, making TOX3 the likely target; however, a T-allele increase in TOX3 expression is a prediction, not shown. GTEx v8 breast eQTL is null at this SNP (E17), and E18a does not provide allele-specific direction.
MCF-7 is the supplied ER-positive luminal breast cancer expression context; GATA3 is highly expressed in MCF-7 and has MCF-7 ChIP occupancy at this element.

The predominant GWAS risk allele is T, including for ER-positive and ER-negative breast cancer, consistent with a T-gain mechanism raising risk; one E15 record with effect allele C requires harmonization, and mediation through GATA3/TOX3 is not shown.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP in heterozygous MCF-7 or breast-derived cells shows more GATA3 on the T allele.
GATA3 depletion or GATA motif disruption reduces T-allele enhancer reporter activity and lowers TOX3 expression.
A breast eQTL or allele-specific expression assay shows higher TOX3 with T; GTEx v8 alone has no significant eQTL at this SNP.
falsified_if: GATA3 ChIP does not show allelic imbalance at rs4784227.
The T allele lowers rather than raises GATA3-dependent enhancer activity or TOX3 expression.
GATA3 knockdown or motif mutation has no effect on this enhancer.

CRISPR editing of this base changes TOX3 expression or a breast cancer-relevant phenotype.

chains.title: FOXA1 binds the alt T allele more strongly and activates a TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: FOXA1 binds the alt T allele more strongly than ref C: E05 shows MCF-7 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant, and E36 gives FOXA1's own QBiC-SELEX model passing the gate with alt-gain (z=9.34, effect=0.314; site strength ref 99.0th vs alt 99.8th percentile); E21 gives a stronger CIS-BP-mapped FOXA2 model (z=15.4, effect=0.296, alt more). The ChIP peak is not allele-specific, so allelic direction is inferred from QBiC-SELEX. FOXA1 is the main competing pioneer-factor explanation because it has matching MCF-7 occupancy, strong expression, and an own-model QBiC alt-gain.

The variant lies in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3180851 with active chromatin marks, so allele-specific FOXA1 binding could change enhancer activity. E03 z-scores are maxima over biosamples, not MCF-7-specific.

The element is assigned to TOX3 by proximity, Open Targets L2G, and literature, making TOX3 the likely target; however, a T-allele increase in TOX3 expression via FOXA1 is a prediction, not shown. GTEx v8 breast eQTL is null at this SNP (E17).
MCF-7 is the ER-positive luminal breast cancer expression context; FOXA1 is expressed in MCF-7 and has MCF-7 ChIP occupancy at this element.

The predominant GWAS risk allele is T, consistent with a T-gain of FOXA1-dependent enhancer activity increasing breast cancer risk; one E15 record with effect allele C requires harmonization, and FOXA1 mediation is not shown.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP in heterozygous MCF-7 cells shows more FOXA1 on the T allele.
FOXA1 depletion or mutation of the FOXA1 motif reduces T-allele enhancer reporter activity and TOX3 expression.
If FOXA1 rather than GATA3 is causal, GATA3 allelic ChIP should not show the same allele-specific effect.
falsified_if: FOXA1 ChIP does not show allelic imbalance at rs4784227.
FOXA1 knockdown or FOXA1 motif mutation does not affect the enhancer or TOX3.
The T allele reduces FOXA1-dependent enhancer activity.

chains.title: NR2F2 binds the alt T allele more strongly at the TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: NR2F2 has MCF-7 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant (E08) and its QBiC-SELEX collection detects an alt-gain change (E22: best model is a CIS-BP-mapped PPARG model, z=9.51, effect=0.22, alt more; site strength ref 95.4th vs alt 97.7th percentile). This is weaker than GATA3/FOXA1 because the best QBiC model is mapped rather than an NR2F2 own model, expression is lower, and no allele-specific ChIP is cited.
The variant is in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3180851, an active element where an NR2F2 binding change could affect enhancer output; E03 z-scores are maxima over biosamples.

The element is linked to TOX3 by proximity and L2G, so an allele-specific NR2F2 effect is predicted to change TOX3 expression; this direction is not demonstrated in breast cells, and GTEx v8 breast eQTL is null.
MCF-7 expresses NR2F2 and has NR2F2 ChIP occupancy at the element, matching the supplied breast cancer expression context.
The T allele is predominantly associated with increased breast cancer risk; if T-allele gain of NR2F2 binding activates TOX3, this could contribute to risk, but mediation is unproven.

predictions: Allele-specific NR2F2 ChIP should show more NR2F2 on the T allele in MCF-7.
NR2F2 depletion should reduce T-allele enhancer activity and TOX3 expression if this chain is correct.
This chain predicts a smaller effect than GATA3/FOXA1 because NR2F2 has lower expression and a mapped QBiC model.
falsified_if: NR2F2 ChIP shows no allelic imbalance at rs4784227.
NR2F2 knockdown has no effect on the enhancer or TOX3.
The NR2F2 motif is not required for the allele-specific enhancer effect.

chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the alt T allele more strongly at the TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: TCF7L2 has a single MCF-7 ChIP-seq peak over the variant (E09) and its QBiC-SELEX collection detects an alt-gain change (E23: best model is a CIS-BP-mapped TCF7 model, z=8.45, effect=0.455, alt more; site strength ref 81.2th vs alt 97.6th percentile). This is weak because TCF7L2 has mapped-model-only QBiC coverage, low expression (4.89 TPM), one ChIP peak, and no allele-specific ChIP.
The variant lies in an active distal enhancer cCRE, so an allele-specific TCF7L2 binding change could alter enhancer activity; E03 z-scores are maxima over biosamples.
The enhancer is assigned to TOX3 by proximity and L2G; T-allele gain of TCF7L2 binding is predicted to increase TOX3 expression, but this is not shown in breast cells and GTEx v8 breast eQTL is null.
MCF-7 is the breast cancer expression context; TCF7L2 is expressed at low level and has MCF-7 ChIP occupancy at this element.
The T allele is predominantly the breast cancer risk allele; TCF7L2-dependent activation of TOX3 would provide an alternative route to risk, but mediation is unproven.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP should show more TCF7L2 on the T allele if this chain is correct.
TCF7L2 depletion should reduce T-allele enhancer activity and TOX3 expression.
Because TCF7L2 expression is low, this chain predicts a weaker effect than GATA3/FOXA1 chains.
falsified_if: TCF7L2 ChIP shows no allelic imbalance at rs4784227.
TCF7L2 knockdown has no effect on the enhancer or TOX3.
The TCF7L2 motif is not required for the allele-specific enhancer effect.

The pooled ORs regarding the association between the rs4784227-CASC16 polymorphism and breast cancer risk were statistically significant [T vs C: OR = 1.244, 95% CI = 1.202-1.287; TT vs CT + CC: OR = 1.407, 95% CI = 1.296-1.528; CC vs CT + TT: OR = 0.777, 95% CI = 0.745-0.811; TT vs CC: OR = 1.544, 95% CI = 1.419-1.681; CT vs CC: OR = 1.244, 95% CI = 1.189-1.301].

Our pooled analysis showed a significant association between the rs4784227- (T) allele and breast cancer susceptibility in Asian and North American populations, and intervention with this mutation might be a new therapeutic strategy for breast cancer.
